en: When Taal Volcano erupts, the fine ash it releases can cause breathing problems, so residents must wear N95 masks outside.
The West Valley Fault runs through Metro Manila, meaning residents must secure heavy furniture to walls to prevent earthquake injuries.
Mount Pulag in Benguet has freezing temperatures at its peak, so hikers must bring thick jackets to prevent hypothermia.
The Pasig River in Metro Manila is heavily polluted, so children should avoid swimming in it to prevent waterborne diseases.
Because the Bicol Region faces the Pacific Ocean directly, residents there must prepare stronger typhoon shelters than those in inland areas.
Swimming in the hot springs of Mount Makiling requires caution because the water temperature can exceed safe limits and cause severe burns.
The Philippines experiences a very high UV index year-round due to its equatorial location, making daily sunscreen use essential for skin health.
Coastal towns in Eastern Samar face higher tsunami risks because they directly border the Pacific Ocean without protective land barriers.
During the Amihan season from November to February, the cooler and drier weather in the Philippines helps reduce mosquito populations and dengue cases.
The Chico River in the Cordillera region flows through steep mountains, so hikers must watch out for sudden flash floods during heavy rains.
Lake Lanao in Mindanao is a crucial freshwater source, so local communities must prevent pollution to ensure a safe drinking water supply.
The steep rice terraces of Ifugao are prone to landslides during heavy rains, so farmers must maintain strong stone walls for safety.
